# The secret merge driver writes the merged plaintext. A symlinked parent
# directory (e.g. a committed `sub -> .git`) must not redirect that write.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp ours.txt $TMPDIR/ours.txt
cp theirs.txt $TMPDIR/theirs.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

mkdir sub
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt sub/config
exec sesam add sub/config --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

exec git checkout -b ours
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt sub/config
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours'

exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt sub/config
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs'

exec git checkout ours
rm sub
mkdir $WORK/trap
symlink sub -> trap

! exec git merge theirs
stderr 'is a symlink'
! exists trap/config

-- base.txt --
first = BASE
last = BASE
-- ours.txt --
first = OURS
last = BASE
-- theirs.txt --
first = BASE
last = THEIRS
